Deliver patch-1 on source v2.

Issue: VotingClassifier.fit raises AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'fit' when sample_weight is passed after an estimator is disabled via set_params(lr=None).

Root cause: in _BaseVoting.fit (sklearn/ensemble/voting.py), the sample_weight support pre-check loop ran has_fit_parameter(step, 'sample_weight') over every (name, step) tuple, including None entries. Only the actual fitting step filtered `clf is not None`, so the None estimator reached attribute lookup and failed.

Fix (1 file, +2 lines in sklearn/ensemble/voting.py): skip None entries in the pre-check loop with `if step is None: continue`, keeping the existing ValueError for real estimators that lack sample_weight support. VotingRegressor shares _BaseVoting.fit and benefits identically.

Evidence: run_tests on sklearn/ensemble/tests/test_voting.py at this exact version (v2, files_sha256 9546247c...) — 18 collected, 18 passed, 0 failed, 0 errors (report test-report-c405da2c2980de6b19936e55, public test sequence 7). Diff reviewed via diff_workspace; net change is only sklearn/ensemble/voting.py. Same-version public evidence only; this is not hidden acceptance.

def test_sample_weight():
    """Tests sample_weight parameter of VotingClassifier"""
    clf1 = LogisticRegression(random_state=123)
    clf2 = RandomForestClassifier(random_state=123)
    clf3 = SVC(gamma='scale', probability=True, random_state=123)
    eclf1 = VotingClassifier(estimators=[
        ('lr', clf1), ('rf', clf2), ('svc', clf3)],
        voting='soft').fit(X, y, sample_weight=np.ones((len(y),)))
    eclf2 = VotingClassifier(estimators=[
        ('lr', clf1), ('rf', clf2), ('svc', clf3)],
        voting='soft').fit(X, y)
    assert_array_equal(eclf1.predict(X), eclf2.predict(X))
    assert_array_almost_equal(eclf1.predict_proba(X), eclf2.predict_proba(X))

                                         ('nb', clf3)],

    eclf2 = VotingClassifier(estimators=[('lr', clf1), ('rf', clf2),
                                         ('nb', clf3)],
                             voting='hard', weights=[1, 1, 0.5])
    eclf2.set_params(rf=None).fit(X, y)
    assert_array_equal(eclf1.predict(X), eclf2.predict(X))

    assert dict(eclf2.estimators)["rf"] is None

    assert_array_almost_equal(eclf1.predict_proba(X), eclf2.predict_proba(X))
    msg = 'All estimators are None. At least one is required!'

        ValueError, msg, eclf2.set_params(lr=None, rf=None, nb=None).fit, X, y)

Deliver patch-2 on source v3 (supersedes patch-1/delivery-1, kept as history).

Issue: VotingClassifier.fit raises AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'fit' when sample_weight is passed and an estimator was disabled via set_params(lr=None).

Root cause: in _BaseVoting.fit (sklearn/ensemble/voting.py) the sample_weight capability pre-check looped over every (name, step) tuple calling has_fit_parameter(step, 'sample_weight'), including None entries. Only the subsequent fit loop filtered `clf is not None`, so the None entry reached attribute lookup first and failed.

Fix (product): skip None entries in the pre-check with `if step is None: continue`, mirroring the fit loop. The existing ValueError for a real estimator that lacks sample_weight support is preserved. VotingRegressor shares _BaseVoting.fit and is fixed identically.

Fix (evidence): added test_sample_weight_none_estimator to sklearn/ensemble/tests/test_voting.py, reproducing the issue verbatim — fit with sample_weight, then set_params(lr=None), then fit with sample_weight again. This closed a real gap: the previously existing tests covered sample_weight (test_sample_weight) and None estimators (test_set_estimator_none) only separately, so the earlier 18/18 run did not exercise the reported bug. The new test asserts fit succeeds and estimators_ has length 1 with 'lr' still None.

Evidence at this exact version (v3, files_sha256 5e37b346...): pytest sklearn/ensemble/tests/test_voting.py — 19 collected, 19 passed, 0 failed, 0 errors, 0 skipped, validation_status verified, exitstatus 0 (report test-report-fd6c03c91817eb2eefe0380c, report sequence 18). Diff reviewed via diff_workspace; changed paths are exactly sklearn/ensemble/voting.py and sklearn/ensemble/tests/test_voting.py.

Not verified: no hidden acceptance suite was run (none is available); the full repository suite was not executed, only the voting module plus its new regression test. Submission is not official acceptance.
